answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake bond before it may trade, like a wharf charging berthing fees before a ship may dock. The bond is slashed if the agent is caught duplicating identities or spamming, so creating a thousand fake accounts costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents recover their stake after a clean record, while an inlet of new identities is throttled so floods cannot overwhelm reviewers. Over time, a grove of bonded identities accumulates reputation that cheap clones cannot buy, raising the attacker's cost above any gain from the fraud.
